how: Pre-register before looking at data: test-data/claim-tests/README.md. Log results with delphi_log_test_result or a pull request. `scouting` says where the data are (test-data/dataset-scouting/COVERAGE.md).

claims.title: Man has eight ribs on each side
claims.statement: The human trunk has eight ribs on each side.

claims.title: All cetaceans are viviparous, never carrying eggs
claims.statement: The dolphin, the whale and all other cetaceans (animals with a blow-hole instead of gills) are viviparous, carrying an embryo rather than eggs, as do humans and viviparous quadrupeds.

claims.title: Some ants fly and others do not
claims.statement: Among ants some fly and others do not, so Flying versus Walking cannot be used to divide animal kinds.

claims.title: Horses gestate a year, humans ten months, elephants two years
claims.statement: Horses and their kin carry their young for a year, man at most ten months, and elephants for two years.

claims.title: Humans gain half their adult height in about the first five years
claims.statement: In human beings the body gains in about the first five years half the height that it gains in all the rest of life.

claims.title: The dolphin, being viviparous, has bones rather than fish-spines
claims.statement: The dolphin, being viviparous, has bones and not fish-spines.

claims.title: The gestation period of both horse and ass is one year
claims.statement: The period of gestation in both the horse and the ass is one year, so the mother gives birth in the same season as she was impregnated.

claims.title: All hair-coated animals are viviparous
claims.statement: Every animal with a coat of hair (counting the spines of hedgehogs and porcupines as hair) bears live young.

claims.title: Wolves and lions have a neck made of a single bone
claims.statement: In all other animals the neck is flexible and has several vertebrae, but in wolves and lions it consists of a single bone.

claims.title: The dolphin has true bone, not fish-spine
claims.statement: The dolphin's skeleton is made of bone, like that of viviparous quadrupeds, not of fish-spine.

claims.title: Dolphins and porpoises suckle their young
claims.statement: The dolphin and the porpoise have milk and suckle their young.

claims.title: Man lives longer than any animal except the elephant
claims.statement: Man lives longer than any animal for which there is credible evidence, except the elephant.

claims.title: The lion's neck is a single bone without vertebrae
claims.statement: The lion's neck consists of a single bone instead of vertebrae.

claims.title: The most children a woman has borne at one birth is five
claims.statement: The largest number of children ever born to a woman at one birth is five, which has been observed several times.

claims.title: Elephant gestation lasts two years with a single calf
claims.statement: The female elephant carries her young for two years and bears only one at a time.

claims.title: The seal has no external ears, only hearing passages
claims.statement: The seal, though a viviparous quadruped, has no external ears but only passages for hearing, because it lives in the water.

claims.title: The redbreast and the redstart are one bird in two seasonal forms
claims.statement: The robin (a winter bird) and the redstart (a summer bird) change into one another and differ only in plumage colour; likewise the beccafico and the blackcap.

claims.title: Crawfish and crabs have ten feet including the claws
claims.statement: The crawfish has five feet on each side including the claws, and the crab likewise has ten feet in all including the claws.

claims.title: Camel gestation lasts twelve months with a single young
claims.statement: The camel carries its young for twelve months and never bears more than one at a time.

claims.title: The cuckoo is not a transformed hawk
claims.statement: The cuckoo is not a transformed hawk: it lacks the hawk's crooked talons, resembles the pigeon in head and claws, and is preyed on by hawks, which never happens between birds of one kind.

claims.title: The heart has three cavities, the right largest and the left smallest
claims.statement: The heart has three cavities: the right-hand one is the largest, the left-hand one the smallest, and the middle one intermediate in size.

claims.title: The river crocodile alone among these animals has no tongue
claims.statement: All oviparous quadrupeds and serpents have a tongue in the mouth except the river crocodile, which has only a space where a tongue would be.

claims.title: Wolves, lions, dogs and leopards have five front toes and four hind
claims.statement: Some polydactylous quadrupeds, such as wolves, lions, dogs and leopards, have five digits on each forefoot but only four on each hind foot.

claims.title: Cuttlefish and squid have an internal shell; the octopus has none
claims.statement: Cuttlefishes have an internal hard part (the os sepiae) and calamaries (squids) the gladius, but poulps (octopuses) have no such part because their body-sac is short.

claims.title: Scaly fish lay eggs; cartilaginous fish bear live young
claims.statement: Scaly fishes are always oviparous, and cartilaginous fishes are all viviparous except the fishing-frog.
